brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb work surface: a center cell plus all six surrounding neighbors
requirements.evidence: Seven full hex base pieces at axial (0,0),(1,0),(1,-1),(0,-1),(-1,0),(-1,1),(0,1), all on level 0 (piece:0,0,0 plus six placed neighbors).
Seven full top covers (addCover, face top) on every cell of the flower.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: 18 caps (addCap) on the 18 exposed outer edges of the six ring cells, three per ring cell; the center cell has no outside edges. The configurator offered exactly these 18 open edges.

finish.summary: Built a 7-cell flower of full hex bases with top covers on all seven cells and 18 edge caps on the perimeter. I also added six joint bolts on the center cell to clear the LOOSE_BODY warning. check_build reports no issues and meshClash "clear". Bolts were not in the brief; they were added only to lock the pieces together.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
